clues.title: Plate: white or yellow, taxi two-tone
text: Peruvian licence plates are either **white** or **yellow**. In contrast to the white plates, yellow plates are less likely to be seen.
Additionally, taxis in Peru typically use licence plates that are [**yellow on the top and white on the bottom**](https://maps.app.goo.gl/K8u6wZg1kdNcwaKs6).
NOTE: Within South America, yellow licence plates are **only** found in Peru, Colombia and rarely, Chile.

images.caption: Peruvian plates: standard white and uncommon yellow

clues.summary: Plates are white or yellow, white being much more common. Taxis often have yellow on top and white below. In South America yellow plates also appear in Colombia and rarely Chile.

clues.title: Google car: solid black or white Gen 3 car
text: In Gen 3 coverage, Peru uses a solid **black** or **white** Google car.
NOTE: In South America, these two cars are limited to the following countries:
- The black Google car is only found in Peru, Argentina and Uruguay.
- The white Google car is only found in Peru, Bolivia and Chile.
clues.summary: Gen 3 uses a solid black or solid white car. Black also appears in Argentina and Uruguay, white in Bolivia and Chile.

clues.title: Google car: Gen 4 exists, unlike its neighbour
text: An important thing to note is that Peru has **Generation 4** Street View coverage, whereas the neighbouring country of Bolivia does not. While Ecuador does have some Generation 4 coverage, it will always have a [large pickup truck](https://maps.app.goo.gl/usxCs6QQVswNua5cA).

images.caption: Mountain valley with a sandy roadside, labelled Generation 4

clues.summary: This country has Gen 4 coverage, but Bolivia does not. Ecuador's Gen 4 always uses a large pickup truck.

differs.how: Ecuador's Gen 4 is a big pickup truck

clues.title: Google car: low Gen 4 'smallcam'
text: Peru also has Generation 4 “smallcam” coverage, which is mounted lower than regular Generation 4 and has a relatively big circular blur with a small protrusion at the front.
NOTE: Peru, Brazil and Argentina are the only South American countries with smallcam.

images.caption: Four panels labelled front panned down, front panned straight, back panned down and good blur (front)

clues.summary: Gen 4 camera mounted lower than usual, with a big round blur and a small bump at the front. In South America only Brazil and Argentina also have it.

clues.title: Road lines: white outer, yellow middle
text: Peruvian roads always have white outer lines. On highways, you will find either **single yellow dashed** or **double yellow** middle lines. On rural mountain roads, you will most likely see white outer lines without any centre line. On divided highways, the road lines may be [completely white](https://maps.app.goo.gl/VLUf8irrxCGb1hTi8) in colour.
NOTE: In the continent of South America, rural mountain roads, with the features mentioned above, are predominantly found in Peru.
clues.summary: Outer lines are always white. Highways have a single dashed or double yellow middle line. Rural mountain roads have white outer lines and no centre line. Divided highways may be all white.

clues.title: Sign: black-and-white striped signposts
text: Peru is the only South American country to use **black-and-white** striped signposts. In some areas, [black-and-yellow](https://goo.gl/maps/4X8W8dd1mmrbhVLH7) signposts can be seen.
NOTE: Uruguay sometimes uses black-and-white posts for its traffic lights, but not for road signs.
clues.summary: The only South American country with black-and-white striped signposts, sometimes black and yellow. Uruguay paints traffic light poles that way, but not sign posts.

differs.how: Uruguay only stripes traffic lights, not sign posts

clues.title: Bollard: red or yellow triangular concrete
text: Bollards in Peru are painted red or yellow, and the country mainly uses a variety of **triangular-shaped** concrete bollards. Occasionally you will also spot other designs, such as these [circular](https://www.google.com/maps/@-14.4839611,-70.9887188,3a,24.9y,19.81h,72.8t/data=!3m6!1e1!3m4!1sU37DGxXpc0hXg0BPOLhRRw!2e0!7i13312!8i6656) concrete variants.
clues.summary: Concrete bollards painted red or yellow, mostly triangular in shape. Round concrete ones appear occasionally.

clues.title: Guardrail: black and yellow stripes
text: **Black-and-yellow** stripes on guardrails are seen throughout the country. You might sometimes find different designs, such as this [sharp arrow](https://goo.gl/maps/Yky9joENHb4taRnr9) design.

NOTE: [Similar striped guardrails](https://goo.gl/maps/aiVM5kgjv2kLebEk9) are also found in Bolivia. To differentiate them, just have a look at the outer stripe. Peru uses a black one, while Bolivia features a yellow one.

images.caption: Black and yellow stripes on the guardrail, marked by the red arrow
Black and yellow stripes on the guardrail, marked by the red arrow

clues.summary: Black-and-yellow striped guardrails are common. Bolivia has similar ones, but look at the outer stripe: black here, yellow in Bolivia.

differs.how: Bolivia's outer stripe is yellow, here it is black

clues.title: Marker: black-and-white concrete km post
text: Kilometre markers in Peru are made out of concrete and are painted black and white.
NOTE: When entering and leaving urban areas, the markers will sometimes feature the [road number](https://goo.gl/maps/yw27rvCrLZj99rDDA).
clues.summary: Kilometre markers are concrete and painted black and white. Near towns they sometimes show the road number.

clues.title: Sign: metal signpost on concrete blocks
text: Peruvian metal signposts feature **concrete blocks** at the bottom.
NOTE: Within South America, Peru is the only country to do so.

images.caption: Red circle marks two white concrete blocks at the base of a green signpost, centre

clues.summary: Metal signposts stand on concrete blocks at the bottom. In South America only this country does that.

clues.title: Pole: concrete or wood, horizontal concrete bars
text: The country uses a variety of poles. They are made out of either **concrete** **or** **wood**, and sometimes feature distinct horizontal concrete bars.
NOTE: Horizontal concrete bars are also found in Argentina.
clues.summary: Poles are concrete or wood, sometimes with distinct horizontal concrete bars. Argentina has those bars too.

clues.title: Pole: painted black or black-yellow bottom
text: Some poles in Peru have **painted bottom sections**. Most commonly they will be black or black-and-yellow.

NOTE: This pattern of pole paint is unique to Peru within South America, however, similar ones can be seen in other South American countries, such as [Colombia](https://maps.app.goo.gl/mMh81AZGJ9zVyYYD7).
clues.summary: Some poles have their bottom section painted black or black and yellow. Unique within South America, though Colombia has similar ones.

clues.title: Bridges: painted orange
text: Bridges in Peru are commonly painted **orange**.
clues.summary: Bridges are commonly painted orange.

clues.title: Landscape: semi-arid mountains and valleys
text: Peru largely consists of semi-arid mountain ranges and valleys.
clues.summary: Mostly semi-arid mountain ranges and valleys.

clues.title: Vehicles: mototaxis (tuk tuks) everywhere
text: **Tuk tuks**, called mototaxis in Peru, are frequently seen in the country, especially in major cities such as Lima, Trujillo, Chiclayo, Piura, and Iquitos.
clues.summary: Three-wheeled mototaxis are frequent, especially in the big cities.

clues.title: Vehicles: wide red and white side stickers
text: **Wide red and white stickers** will typically be attached to the side of taxis and [commercial vehicles](https://maps.app.goo.gl/iucN3Sf5cXq8ZDnu8).
NOTE: While less common, these can be found in some [neighbouring countries](https://maps.app.goo.gl/HX6E3dH1CuCGpdfp6).

images.caption: Circle zooms in on the wide red and white side sticker on the car

clues.summary: Wide red and white stickers on the side of taxis and commercial vehicles. A few neighbouring countries have them less often.

clues.title: Objects: rectangular metal meter with slits
text: Peruvian **electricity counters** have a unique design: They are rectangular, metallic, and typically feature two or three horizontal slits.
clues.summary: Electricity meters are rectangular and metallic, with two or three horizontal slits, a bit like a post box.

clues.title: Currency: 'S/' symbol
text: **Sol** is the currency of Peru. You will occasionally spot it on street view and its symbol is **S/**.
NOTE: The currency is unique to Peru.

images.caption: Circle zooms in on 'DE S/2' on a sign, showing the S/ currency symbol

clues.summary: The currency is the sol, shown as S/, which you can occasionally spot on signs. Unique to this country.

clues.title: Signs: local political party logos
text: Peru has many political party logos and all of them are unique to the country. [Here](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_political_parties_in_Peru) is a list with other parties in Peru.
clues.summary: Many political party logos appear, all unique to the country.

clues.title: Houses: colonial, boxy, red brick
text: Peru is home to diverse and somewhat unique architecture. Here are a few examples of types of buildings commonly seen in Peru; ranging from Colonial-era buildings, contemporary “boxy” buildings, and traditional red brick buildings.
Some of these styles are broken down further in Step 2 of this guide.
clues.summary: Mixed architecture: colonial-era buildings, modern boxy buildings and traditional red brick houses.

clues.title: Coverage: mostly west and main highways
text: Street View coverage in Peru is mostly located in the **west** and on main highways. There are some exceptions in the east near [Iquitos](https://maps.app.goo.gl/3A9MV5GPmjCHimLM7) and along the [30C](https://maps.app.goo.gl/wEQV21hKmorbxVXp7).
_You can click on the image to enlarge it._
clues.summary: Coverage is mostly in the west and on main highways, with a few exceptions in the east near the Amazon city and along road 30C.

clues.title: Landscape: flat east, mountainous west
text: The country is generally flat in the east and mountainous in the west. However, an exception is the often flat desert near Piura in the northwest.
_You can click on the image to enlarge it._
clues.summary: Flat in the east and mountainous in the west, except for a flat desert in the north-west.

clues.title: Landscape: dry desert west, rainforest east
text: Peru has a diverse climate, dominated by a [**dry desert**](https://goo.gl/maps/4XWT67dUk3PGbCAo6) in the west, and a [**tropical rainforest**](https://goo.gl/maps/YRV9ZwPAv3LBSqWM9) in the east.
_You can click on the image to enlarge it._
clues.summary: A dry desert in the west and tropical rainforest in the east.

clues.title: Route numbers: highways in the west, rising south
text: Highways in Peru are mainly located in the west, and the numbers increase from north to south. The 1, 3 and 5 are the longest and traverse through multiple departments.
_You can click on the image to enlarge it._
clues.summary: Highways are mainly in the west with numbers rising from north to south. Routes 1, 3 and 5 are the longest.

clues.title: Landscape: sandy soil, green or withered bushes
text: These three landscapes are typically found along offroads in Tumbes. You will always see sandy soil with either **green or withered bushes**.
NOTE: In addition, Tumbes does not have black cars on off roads. Make sure to consider it whenever you see such landscapes with a white Street View car.
clues.summary: Off-road tracks in the far north-west have sandy soil with green or dry bushes. No black cars there, so a white car fits.

clues.title: Landscape: dry, flat, few shrubs, some rolling hills
text: The southwestern landscape of Piura is generally dry, featuring a **low amount of vegetation** with a few shrubs and bushes. The landscape is mostly flat, but you will sometimes see rolling hills.
clues.summary: In the south-west of one northern region: dry, mostly flat land with few shrubs and sometimes rolling hills.

clues.title: Landscape: same dry shrubs but noticeably hillier
text: Northwest of the city of Piura lies an area with similar vegetation to the area mentioned previously. However, this area is **noticeably hillier**.
clues.summary: North-west of that city, similar plants but noticeably hillier.

clues.title: Plants: coconut palms in coastal farmland
text: **Coconut palms** (and other species of tall palms) can sometimes be seen in coastal areas of Peru, mainly north of Lima. They are mainly found in the agricultural areas which are typically found around the major coastal cities.
clues.summary: Coconut and other tall palms in coastal farm areas, mainly north of the capital.

clues.title: Plants: olive plantations in the far south
text: **Olive tree plantations** can be found in the far southern region of Tacna.
clues.summary: Olive tree plantations in the far southern region.

clues.title: Farming: big sugar cane fields on the north coast
text: Most of the **sugar cane** production is found in the northern coastal regions of Peru near the cities of Chiclayo and Trujillo. Typically you see **large fields** of sugar cane in these areas. Smaller areas of sugar cane can be found further south in other valleys close to the Pacific coast.
clues.summary: Most sugar cane is on the northern coast near two big cities, in large fields. Smaller areas appear in southern coastal valleys.

clues.title: Farming: banana plants near the north coast
text: Similarly to sugar cane plants, **banana plants** are generally found in agricultural regions adjacent to the coast in the northern half of the country.
clues.summary: Banana plants grow in farmland near the coast in the northern half.

clues.title: Landscape: flat highland plain
text: A** flat landscape** in the mountains of Peru is usually seen in central Puno and around Lake Chinchaycocha.
NOTE: This landscape might look similar to Bolivia. Make sure to look out for other clues before guessing.

images.caption: Flat highland plain; a red circle and arrow mark the distant lake and hills on the horizon.

clues.summary: A flat landscape in the mountains, mostly in central Puno and around a high marshy lake. It can look like Bolivia.

clues.title: Landscape: low grass, stone walls, brown brick
text: Low grass, a few hills, stone walls in villages and brown brick buildings are typical for the region south of **Lake Titicaca** in eastern Peru.
clues.summary: Low grass, a few hills, stone-walled villages and brown brick buildings, south of a huge high-altitude lake.

clues.title: Landscape: shrubby mountains, dry near the coast
text: Far north Peru features mountains that are often covered in **shrubby trees and bushes**. Closer to the coast and the Ecuador border, these mountains are often [quite dry](https://maps.app.goo.gl/2sAyUVLu4AdVCyuc7#extra%5Btags%5D=Sandy+Orange&extra%5BloadMode%5D=latLng) in appearance.
clues.summary: In the far north, mountains often covered in shrubby trees and bushes. Closer to the coast and the border they look quite dry.

clues.title: Plants: pine plantations at altitude
text: **Pine plantations** are typically** **found in higher elevation areas of the country, away from the coastal deserts and Amazonian Regions. The most common types of pine trees planted are [Pinus radiata](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pinus_radiata) and [Pinus patula](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pinus_patula).
clues.summary: Pine plantations in higher areas, away from the coastal desert and Amazon, mostly two planted species.

clues.title: Landscape: medium foliage-covered mountains, Amazon
text: The areas adjacent to the northern Amazonian city of Tarapoto feature **moderately tall foliage-covered mountains** and can bear a similar resemblance to the hilly areas of [Colombia](https://maps.app.goo.gl/9CLDvLq2CxSaRJqE8) or [Brazil](https://maps.app.goo.gl/wcxWAuqehRqPfCm96).
clues.summary: Around a northern Amazon city: moderately tall mountains covered in foliage, resembling hilly parts of Colombia or Brazil.

clues.title: Landscape: exposed rock outcrops in hillsides
text: In higher elevation areas near the centre of the country, **exposed rocky outcroppings** are commonly seen in the sides of hills and mountains. Some areas with the highest concentrations are near Lago Chinchaycocha (Junin District) stretching south towards the city of Ayacucho.
NOTE: Exposed rocks can rarely be seen anywhere in the country, so use this meta with some caution.
clues.summary: In higher areas near the centre, bare rock outcrops on hill and mountain sides. Densest from a high lake south toward a southern city. They are rare elsewhere, so be careful.

clues.title: Landscape: tall mountains with sharp rocky tops
text: Similarly, taller mountains near the middle of the country often feature **rocky and sharp mountain tops**. The main region of these mountains stretches from near the city of Huaraz southward to the city of Cusco; generally away from the coast.
clues.summary: Taller central mountains often have rocky, sharp tops, stretching from the north-central city south to the big southern tourist city, away from the coast.

clues.title: Plants: light green lichen on rocks
text: Patches of **light green **[**lichen**](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lichen) can be seen covering rocks and growing on the ground in high elevation areas of central and southern Peru.
clues.summary: Patches of light green lichen cover rocks and ground at high elevations in the centre and south.

clues.title: Soil: dark red-tinted
text: **Dark red-tinted soil** is found in several areas of Peru. Some notable areas include the areas near Cusco and Ayacucho in the south of the country, as well as areas near the northern cities of Cajamarca and Tarapoto. It can be found to a lesser extent in adjacent regions.
clues.summary: Dark red-tinted soil near several southern and northern cities, and a bit in neighbouring regions.

clues.title: Landscape: barren flat desert with mountains east
text: Areas near the cities of Ica, Arequipa, and Tacna feature** barren and mostly flat desert landscapes** that can resemble areas of [northern Chile](https://goo.gl/maps/LF4MFBiVCeULmxmT7). You can typically see mountains in the distance, primarily while looking to the east.
clues.summary: Barren, mostly flat desert near three southern cities. Mountains show in the distance, mainly to the east. It can resemble northern Chile.

clues.title: Landscape: farm valleys between bare mountains
text: Coastal **agricultural valleys** in the middle and south are commonly sandwiched between **dry mountains with no vegetation**. The general orientation of these valleys are southwest-northeast.
NOTE: Agricultural valleys in the north of Peru can look similar, but often feature more shrubs and trees on the mountains.
clues.summary: In the middle and south, farm valleys run south-west to north-east between dry mountains with no plants. Northern ones look similar but have more shrubs and trees on the mountains.

clues.title: Houses: red brick, more near the big lake
text: As a general rule, the closer you are to Lake Titicaca in Peru, houses and buildings made out of **red brick** become more common. This type of architecture resembles the predominant type of building seen in parts of [western Bolivia](https://goo.gl/maps/qNyBR5RytYNpUZHg8), which is helpful for remembering where it is seen most commonly. Additionally, buildings with [blue tinted glass](https://maps.app.goo.gl/rS2S5g3xNuSUF9k89#extra%5BloadMode%5D=latLng) can be seen most commonly in the same areas.
NOTE: Red brick buildings can be seen anywhere in the country, so use other clues before guessing.
clues.summary: Red brick houses become more common near the big high lake, like western Bolivia. Blue-tinted glass is common there too. Red brick appears anywhere, so check other clues.

clues.title: Houses: overhanging roofs on wooden supports
text: Buildings with **overhanging roofs with wooden supports** are mostly found in northern regions of Peru. These buildings are sometimes brightly coloured as well.
clues.summary: Overhanging roofs with wooden supports, sometimes bright colours, mostly in the north.

clues.title: Pole: yellow vertical numbers, north coast
text: Pole markings with **yellow vertical numbers** are commonly found in northern coastal Peru and Tacna.

Oftentimes, but not always, they will be accompanied by a horizontal pole marking starting with a 2 or 3 letter code corresponding to a city. For example, this horizontal sticker starts with CH for Chimbote.

NOTE: you can further divide the region based on the number of digits and the actual numbers on the pole marking. See [this document](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1rMBXs3_grdmPBdzT1fSfkj-MEnagQylqJnlbqOXBwkE/edit) for details.

images.caption: A pole with yellow vertical numbers

clues.summary: Yellow vertical pole numbers on the northern coast and the far south, often with a horizontal sticker starting with a 2 or 3 letter city code, like CH.

clues.title: Vehicles: tuk tuks with open front
text: Tuk-Tuks with **open front compartments** are primarily found in the northern half of Peru, and are especially common in northern Amazonian adjacent regions.
NOTE: This type of Tuk-Tuk can be found elsewhere to a lesser extent, so use other clues before guessing.
clues.summary: Tuk tuks with an open front compartment, mostly in the northern half, especially near the northern Amazon.

clues.title: Lamp posts: inverted J curve at the top
text: Lamp posts in Lima and Lima Department often have a distinct, sweeping curve at the top, resembling an **inverted "J" shape**.
NOTE: This design can occasionally be found in other parts of the country, such as Iquitos and Pucallpa.
For other, more specific patterns, please see this [document](https://docs.google.com/presentation/d/18VA4IlPGHCrfpYif-aBEsAanjBdm5vPyoPr5Wqjpf7g/).
clues.summary: Street lamp posts in the capital region often curve at the top like an upside-down J. Also occasionally in two Amazon cities.

clues.title: Bollard: cylindrical, black-and-yellow stripe on top
text: This cylindrical bollard, with a **black and yellow stripe at the top**, is unique to the state of Moquegua, which is located in the south of Peru.
clues.summary: A cylindrical bollard with black and yellow stripe at the top, unique to one southern region. It can look round and white with orange and black marks on top.

clues.title: Landscape: semidesert, overcast Gen 3
text: The 1N near the Piura and Lambayeque border has a distinct looking landscape. It features a semidesert landscape and has overcast coverage in Generation 3. The new Generation 4 is drier but still looks somewhat similar.

images.caption: Upper photo: a semi-desert road under overcast sky.

clues.summary: Road 1N near the border of two northern regions: semidesert and overcast in Gen 3. Gen 4 is drier but looks similar.

clues.title: Road: divided highway on the coast
text: Highway 1N/S is **divided** in the highlighted area on the map.
NOTE: It is the **only** divided highway outside of cities.
clues.summary: Highway 1 is divided in the highlighted area, the only divided highway outside cities.

clues.title: Road: undivided coastal highway, red soil, Gen 4
text: The 1S south of the city of Ica is **not divided** and mostly follows the coast. The soil is often red or orange in these areas, and there is little-to-no vegetation. This road is also entirely covered with the **Generation 4** camera.
clues.summary: Road 1S south of the southern desert city is not divided and follows the coast. Soil is often red or orange with almost no plants, and it is all Gen 4.

clues.title: Road: straight flat good road through rainforest
text: **Ruta 5N **between the towns of San Alejandro and Esperanza is a relatively straight, flat road in good condition. This road primarily runs north-south through the rainforest.
clues.summary: Road 5N is a straight, flat road in good condition, running north-south through rainforest.

clues.title: Google car: white Gen 3 car, jungle road
text: **Ruta 30C** in eastern Peru uses a white Street View car in Generation 3 between the cities of Planchon and Iñapari. It features dense forest, few villages, and resembles interior areas of Brazil. Some of this area has been overwritten with [Generation 4](https://www.google.com/maps/@-11.5434488,-69.2916923,3a,90y,170.18h,87.56t/data=!3m6!1e1!3m4!1sp8bJgFNzPpFzeqeYQxMyJA!2e0!7i16384!8i8192). Most of this segment runs north to south.
clues.summary: Road 30C in the east has a white Gen 3 car with dense forest and few villages, resembling interior Brazil. Parts are overwritten by Gen 4.

clues.title: Road: small, faded lines, hillside above river
text: **Ruta 28B **between the towns of Kimbiri and Echarate is a paved road with very faded or missing road lines. It is also characterised by being a relatively small road with Generation 4 coverage, which hugs the hillside and is located next to a river valley.
clues.summary: Road 28B is a small paved road with faded or missing lines in Gen 4, hugging a hillside next to a river valley.

clues.title: Landscape: flat plain with trees and villages
text: The valley connecting the cities of Jauja and Huancayo features a flat plain with **plentiful trees, agricultural areas, and small villages**. North-south oriented mountains can be seen on both edges of the valley.
clues.summary: The valley between two central cities is a flat plain with plenty of trees, farms and small villages, with north-south mountains on both sides.

clues.title: Coverage: wetter season north of the big lake
text: The coverage on the north side of Lake Titicaca was taken during a significantly wetter season than the coverage taken on the south side of Lake Titicaca.
clues.summary: Coverage north of the big lake was taken in a much wetter season than the south side.

clues.title: Landscape: marshy shallow lake with mountains east
text: North of the city of Huancayo lies a shallow lake called Lake Chinchaycocha (also referred to as ‘the middle lake.’). This lake is generally** marshy** and a **range of mountains** can be seen to the** east **of the lake. This lake can look similar to Lake Titicaca, but is generally less densely populated and features fewer trees.
clues.summary: A shallow marshy lake with a mountain range to the east. It looks like the big high lake, but has fewer people and trees.

clues.title: Landscape: volcanoes near the southern city
text: **Volcanoes** are often seen in and around the city of Arequipa.
NOTE: Within Peru, volcanoes are **only** found in the southeast in the highlighted area.
clues.summary: Volcanoes are often seen around one southern city. In this country they are only in the south-east.

clues.title: Streets: long straight boulevards with median
text: Most of the boulevard-type streets in Peru are in the city of Lima. These boulevards are typically **long, straight streets **divided by** concrete** or a** grassy berm**.
clues.summary: Boulevard-style streets, mostly in the capital: long, straight, divided by concrete or a grassy strip.

clues.title: Streets: grid running WSW to ENE
text: The east-central Amazonian city of Pucallpa, which lies close to the Brazil border, has a consistent **street grid** of **WSW to ENE**.
NOTE: Some northern and eastern areas of the city feature grids of different orientation.
clues.summary: An Amazon city near the Brazil border has a consistent street grid running west-south-west to east-north-east, though some northern and eastern areas differ.

clues.title: Coverage: isolated Amazon city, Gen 3 only
text: Iquitos is a city in **northeast Peru**. It is an isolated city with only **Generation 3** Street View coverage. [Three-wheeled tuk-tuks](https://goo.gl/maps/sF5AYaumuA4RzSnP8), overcast skies, and [rolling Amazonian landscapes](https://goo.gl/maps/f1Jx1vsQcHc44o3w7) are commonly seen in the area. This coverage is isolated from other areas of northern Peru.
clues.summary: A remote north-east city with only Gen 3 coverage: tuk tuks, overcast skies and rolling Amazon landscapes. It is cut off from other northern coverage.

clues.title: Houses: red brick and colonial, mountains all around
text: The southern city of Cusco is recognizable by its prevalence of both [red brick](https://goo.gl/maps/SPo96ELYh9L8WLkX9) and [Spanish colonial style](https://goo.gl/maps/gEzLN3km1TnyiaUk8) buildings. Cusco is surrounded by **mountains on all sides** and features an [**airport in the middle of the city**](https://goo.gl/maps/Dxg9TFTNUNZZCxAVA). Due to its proximity and similar architecture, Cusco superficially resembles the Bolivian city of [La Paz](https://goo.gl/maps/4QxcjEmUPQeAFLjf9).
clues.summary: A southern city with lots of red brick and Spanish colonial buildings, mountains on all sides and an airport in the middle. It resembles La Paz in Bolivia.

clues.title: Landscape: dry ridge north of a southern city
text: The city of Tacna in the far south of Peru has this distinct **dry** **ridge **to the north.
clues.summary: A distinct dry ridge to the north of the far-southern city.

clues.title: People: motorcycle taxi drivers in yellow vests
text: **Motorcycle taxi** drivers in the Amazonian city of Puerto Maldonado can often be seen wearing **yellow safety vests**.
clues.summary: In one Amazon city, motorcycle taxi drivers often wear yellow safety vests.

clues.title: Google car: white car on the route to ruins
text: Within Peru, this **white** Street View car is found in central Cusco. It drives from the remote town of Aguas Calientes up to Machu Picchu.
clues.summary: A white Street View car drives from a remote town up to the famous mountain ruins, in the Cusco area.

clues.title: Coverage: trekker along a train track
text: A **train track** covered by a trekker is located between Aguas Calientes and Cusco.
clues.summary: A trekker covers a train track between a remote town and the Cusco area.

clues.title: Pole: yellow sticker with sideways black numbers
text: In the wider Cusco area and up to the tri-point with Brazil and Bolivia, concrete poles will sometimes have yellow stickers with black numbers going sideways.

clues.title: Landscape: flat jungle, no mountains, good road
text: The 18C and 5N road in central Peru, south and east from Pucalipa, and the 30C in eastern Peru, curving up to the Bolivian border, are pretty much the only places in the country with a flat profile (no visible mountains), a well-built road, and lush, jungly vegetation with a slightly yellow tint. You can tell which of the two you're on from the clouds: there aren't really any on the 30C, and the 18C/5N will always have substantial clouds.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.summary: Roads 18C/5N and 30C are almost the only places with a flat profile, no mountains, a good road and lush, slightly yellow-tinted jungle. 30C has almost no clouds, 18C/5N always has big clouds.

clues.title: Bollard: Moquegua colours in other prism shapes
text: Bollards with the same color scheme as the Moquegua ones, but in different prism shapes (triangular, quadrangular) and/or with white and red reflectors appear on the 38A through Tacla and Puno and on the 3S south of Ilave. If they appear in Gen 3 coverage, go Ilo (on the coast)

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.summary: Bollards with the black, yellow and white scheme of the southern region's bollards, but triangular or square, sometimes with white and red reflectors, on the 38A through Tacna and Puno and the 3S south of Ilave. In Gen 3 it points to the coastal town Ilo.

clues.title: Bollard: half-buried bollards and loose white rocks
text: Around the town of Locumba, between Moquegua and Tacna, you get bollards that look like half-buried Moquegua type, interspersed with sections with just loose white rocks for bollards.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.summary: Around Locumba, between two southern regions, bollards look like half-buried versions of the southern type, mixed with sections of just loose white rocks.

clues.title: Coverage: dark red sunset, eerie clouds
text: East of Chimbote, there's a road where sundown and clouds conspired to create footage as if from the depths (or rather heights?) of hell.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.summary: East of one coastal city, a road where the sunset and clouds made the footage look hellish.

clues.title: Road: black Gen 3 car, no centre line, Amazon hills
text: The road to Iquitos can be recognized by **black car Gen 3**, **lack of center lines** and **rolling Amazonian landscape**

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.summary: The road to the Amazon city shows a black Gen 3 car, no centre lines and rolling Amazon landscape.

clues.title: Bollard: only on the highway north of the capital
text: This bollard is only found on the 1N highway north of Lima (still within Lima region).

clues.title: Bollard: only on the coast road between two cities
text: These bollards are only found on the 1S highway between the towns of Ica and Lima.

clues.summary: These bollards appear only on the 1S highway between Ica and the capital.

clues.title: Bollard: almost only in the far south
text: This bollard is almost exclusive to Tacna region. It does spill into Moquegua but it is by far most common in Tacna.

clues.summary: This bollard is almost only in the far-southern region, spilling a bit into its neighbour.
